brief: GS's Pasquariello frames a tricky week for US equities: the S&P has been flat for three months (60-day realized vol near 10%, bottom-quartile for the COVID/post-COVID era), yet a muted 47bp weekly move hid renewed pain in GS's hedge fund VIP pair trade, because the market is hammering consensus positions for reasons he splits evenly between positioning and fundamentals. On positioning, a strong first half including an epic Q2 gave way to a drawdown since end-June as heavy AI-theme length unwound; GS's own book saw sustained net-and-gross de-risking, Thursday's tech selling the heaviest in two years, which he reads as possible capitulation. On fundamentals, skepticism has hit the AI narrative even as mega-cap demand holds up, because the market is questioning the buildout's power and capital supply. Oil's breakout and midterm risk add further pressure. He has limited conviction and is swimming closer to shore, though he notes this pattern (a month of de-risking, firmer implied vol, a first-since-March negative Risk Appetite Indicator) historically precedes improved risk/reward. Hyperscaler earnings next week are pivotal; GS still forecasts 18% 2027 EPS growth, keeping the bull trend intact but flatter. Separately, corporate credit is melting down.
